paper.title_en: Dust matter cosmology in modified symmetric teleparallel $f(Q,T)$ gravity
paper.abstract_en: We investigate the nonlinear $f(Q,T)$ gravity model, $f(Q,T) = αQ^n + βT + γ$, which represents a nontrivial coupling between geometry and matter in the context of a dust-dominated Universe. The model parameters $(H_0, α, β, γ, n)$ are constrained using recent cosmological observations, including Hubble parameter measurements $H(z)$, the Pantheon+SH0ES dataset, and DESI BAO data. The analysis shows that the Hubble constant exhibits dataset-dependent variations, reflecting the persisting Hubble tension, while $α$ and $γ$ are tightly constrained and $β$ remains weakly determined. The nonlinear exponent $n$ introduces an additional degree of freedom that enhances the model's flexibility in reproducing observational trends. The cosmographic diagnostics, including the deceleration, jerk, snap, and lerk parameters, indicate a Universe transitioning from early deceleration to late-time acceleration, with present values closely aligned with $Λ$CDM predictions and far-future behavior approaching a de Sitter phase. These results demonstrate that the nonlinear $f(Q,T)$ model provides a simple and viable framework to describe late-time cosmic acceleration, accommodate observational tensions, and reproduce $Λ$CDM-like dynamics with subtle deviations.
